scenario.title: Landing work, merge review and merge queues
situations: A verified change is ready to land.
A queued pull request stops, its base changes, or required checks disagree.
The user asks which commit actually landed and whether it was reviewed.
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
questions: Audit merge candidate review, human review and queue CI reuse as distinct contracts; current map mentions approvals/QA but does not trace this complete landing family.

lessons.title: Explain the current landing route
lessons.when: When an item reaches its merge boundary or the project first enables a merge queue.
lessons.need: Know whether this item lands locally or through a governed pull request/queue, what proof the route uses, and which result proves landing.
lessons.surface: Merge item; merge-review candidate; merge receipt/landing reads; GitHub queue readiness
lessons.gap: Existing sources and commands are present; scenario-to-first-explanation timing has not been traced. Review question: should JOURNEYS add first-landing and first-queue-use situations?

lessons.title: Resume a stopped landing without inventing success
lessons.when: When a landing notice reports a stopped queue, failed check or unavailable automatic wake.
lessons.need: Identify the actual check/protection/ownership problem and the supported same-item recovery; a green check is not itself a merge receipt. Standalone close-out waits only for push-owned checks. A cancelled push follows a proven descendant with replacement push workflows, reports the superseding SHA and retains the original deadline.
lessons.surface: Landing notice, holder/steering recovery and governed merge re-entry
lessons.gap: A recovery guide exists. Review question: do each harness notice and FIRST-USER 35 output link the correct recovery without implying universal automatic desktop wake?
